messages:
liam: Heads-up — saw steady memory growth on a long streaming chat session that triggers a tool-loop (repeated tool calls appending context). Not leaking libc objects, but KV cache resident pages keep increasing even after the session ends. Repro on staging with low qps.

maria: ugh. do you have jemalloc stats + pmap / proc/maps from the run? also which model/seq-len distribution?

liam: paste of quick stats from the failing run:
```
jemalloc.stats: allocated=1.2GB active=2.8GB mapped=3.1GB
kv_cache: entries=4123 resident_pages=87264 reclaimed_pages=1632
proc/mem: RSS=2.9G VSZ=4.1G
last_gc: none (session ended but cache didn't drop)
```
model: llama-2-13b, avg seq=18k tokens during stream; tool loop does: call tool -> append tool output -> continue generation (tiny responses each loop).

devon: quick hypothesis: fragmentation + page handoff when we expand small kv slabs into larger buckets, causing pages to remain pinned. Could be the slab allocator's "handoff" path failing to coalesce after many small inserts/evicts.

anita: also worth checking eviction policy. If there's a long-lived session pointer keeping a view into KV (iterator/reader), eviction will skip entries and resident_pages won't go down. Any long-lived iterators in the tool loop?

liam: I grep'd for open iterators — we keep a session cursor per stream, but it's reset each turn. I can't find anything obviously holding references post-session.

maria: next steps: 1) run a controlled repro with debug flags: KV_DEBUG=1 KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.5 KV_SLAB_DUMP=1 2) collect perf + heaptrack of the runtime during a repro 3) force a manual eviction and observe page counts.

liam: running repro with flags now. command I'm using:
```
./repro-runner --scenario streaming-tool-loop --iterations 100 
export KV_DEBUG=1 KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.5 KV_SLAB_DUMP=1
./start-load.sh --clients 2
```
I'll share logs/pprof when complete.

devon: add a run toggling kernel selection path too (we saw different allocation patterns when using optimized attention kernels under high seq lengths). set RUNTIME_KERNEL=fast_attn_v2 vs baseline. might change the allocation stride.

liam: good call. doing both variants.

anita: if this repro is fast, try running with malloc_conf:lg_dirty_mult settings for jemalloc to see if reducing dirty pages helps. also try enabling the new slab coalescer branch locally (dev branch: slab-coalesce/2026).

liam: results (short): forcing eviction threshold to 0.5 drops resident_pages during run, but after session end pages creep back up slowly. slab dump shows repeated small free fragments in same slab groups — they aren't being reused for new kv objects (aligned sizes mismatch?).

maria: can you paste a snippet of the slab dump?

liam: snippet:
```
SLAB group size=64B: allocated=1024 free_fragments=128 fragments_in_use=896
SLAB group size=512B: allocated=256 free_fragments=12 fragments_in_use=244
SLAB group size=2048B: allocated=64 free_fragments=0 fragments_in_use=64
reclaimable_pages: [0x7f9a1, 0x7f9a3, 0x7f9a9 ...] (lots of holes)
```
Looks like many tiny fragments in 64B blocks; new kv entries trend to ~80-120B so we should reuse 128B bucket but allocator is rounding differently.

devon: sounds like a bucket-sizing bug after kernel path changes — the allocator might be requesting slightly larger ranges (alignment/padding change) causing mismatch with slab freelists. Check the code path where we serialize KV entries (padding + checksum).

anita: if we can't fix quickly, mitigation: garbage-collect slabs periodically for long sessions, or trigger a background defrag pass that tries to consolidate free fragments into reusable chunks. We should add a metric for "fragmentation ratio" and alert on >0.6 over 10m.

liam: created a short reproducer github gist and a perf flamegraph link: https://internal/gists/1865432100 and https://perf/fg/1865432100. Perf shows a lot of time in slab allocator hot path around append/reserve.

maria: nice. can you also run valgrind/heaptrack build once to be absolutely sure it's not a pointer leak path? I know slower but worth it for a 1-off.

liam: started heaptrack run. will upload. preliminary verdict: not a pointer leak; allocator internal fragmentation + failure to reuse particular bucket sizes.

devon: next engineering action items: 1) add detailed kv allocation histogram (size vs bucket vs slab-id) 2) add forced defrag + test harness for long streaming sessions 3) review kernel selection changes for padding/align differences 4) consider bumping eviction aggressiveness for sessions flagged as "continuous tool loop".

anita: I'll file a tracking ticket and assign to devon/liam with logs and repro. ticket: INF-1742 (kv slab fragmentation: long-stream tool loop).

ops-bot: repro-runner completed: iterations=100 duration=18m rss_peak=3.2G resident_pages_end=89512 resident_pages_postgc=88040 (background defrag reduced ~1.6%) :white_check_mark:

liam: thanks all — will follow up with heaptrack + stack traces. tagging @maria for eviction heuristics review and @devon for allocator/path changes. :thumbsup:
